Alerts when tracked displacement reaches your threshold in camera pixels (px; say: PIK-suhlz).
Alerts on current smoothed acceleration in g (standard gravity; say: jee), matching this graph. Root mean square (RMS; say: ar-em-ess) status labels use separate thresholds.

One alert per crossing. Waits 3 seconds, then rearms below 90% of the threshold. The alert sound plays for up to 2.5 seconds. Sound and vibration follow phone settings. Feedback can affect both graphs; turn it off for clean measurements.

Enable alerts separately in Visual and Physical and apply a positive threshold. Visual uses tracked displacement in px; Physical uses current smoothed acceleration in g, matching the graph, not RMS or frequency. The dashed line marks the applied threshold. Sound and phone vibration can be switched off independently; the last-alert message still appears. Alerts work on every tab while monitoring in the foreground. Reaching or exceeding a threshold triggers once; holding above it does not repeat. Both alerts pause for 3 seconds after a trigger. Feedback disarms both channels until each has a fresh reading below 90% of its threshold after that pause. Crossings during the pause are not queued. Sound and vibration can move the phone and contaminate readings, including peak and Hz; the cooldown prevents repeated alerts but does not remove those readings. Use feedback off for clean measurements. Stop, backgrounding, or camera failure cancels feedback. Settings survive tab switches and sessions, but are not saved after the app process closes. These are user-selected alerts, not calibrated safety limits.

Hz is hertz (say: hurts), meaning cycles per second: 10 Hz means about 10 repetitions each second. This estimates the strongest repeating component of the phone’s acceleration, not the remote marker’s motion or necessarily a machine’s rotation speed. It uses 2 seconds of signed, gravity-suppressed sensor axes and refreshes twice per second, in 0.5 Hz steps. The nominal range is 2–40 Hz; slower or uneven sampling lowers the upper limit. Observed sensor rate is samples per second, not vibration frequency. Weak motion, irregular shakes, or multiple competing frequencies may show —. Sensor gaps over 0.05 seconds restart collection; stopping also clears the estimate. Out-of-range vibration can alias into a misleading lower frequency. This prototype estimate still needs comparison with a known-frequency source.
Full names and how to say them

m/s² — meters per second squared. Read the full phrase aloud; it measures acceleration.
m/s — meters per second; speed.
m² — square meters; area. The squared part of m/s² applies to seconds, not meters.
g — acceleration relative to standard gravity. Say: jee. It does not mean grams here.
Hz — hertz. Say: hurts. One hertz means one cycle per second.
RMS — root mean square. Say: ar-em-ess. An overall vibration level.
px — pixels. Say: PIK-suhlz. Tiny elements of the camera image.
s — seconds. Say: SEK-uhndz.
ms — milliseconds. Say: MIL-ih-sek-uhndz. 1,000 milliseconds = 1 second.
mm — millimeters. Say: MIL-ih-mee-terz. MotionX does not measure distance in millimeters.
X / Y / Z — axis labels, not abbreviations. Say: ex / why / zed.
Peak — highest level, not an abbreviation. Say: peek.
Accelerometer — acceleration sensor. Say: ak-SEL-uh-ROM-ih-ter.
Pronunciations are written hints; they do not play audio.
Camera ready → START MONITORING → both sensors run. Switching tabs changes the view; both keep monitoring while the app is in the foreground. Expand a diagram below.
Rear camera\nCapture images of a black marker
Find and track the marker\nRead its X / Y position in the camera image
Compare with the starting position\nCalculate displacement in camera pixels (px; say: PIK-suhlz)
Display displacement + live 10-second graph\nSend valid px readings to the Visual alert check
Marker lost? Show unavailable and a graph gap; skip the alert check. Finding the marker again sets a new starting position. Keep the camera steady.
Phone accelerometer (say: ak-SEL-uh-ROM-ih-ter)\nRead X / Y / Z (ex / why / zed) in meters per second squared (m/s²), including gravity
Estimate and subtract gravity\nConvert the remaining acceleration to g (standard gravity; say: jee)
MOTION LEVEL\nMagnitude → smoothing → current g (standard gravity; say: jee)\nFeeds the 10-second graph, session peak and Physical alert check
OVERALL LEVEL\nUnsmoothed magnitude → rolling root mean square (RMS; say: ar-em-ess)\nRMS determines NORMAL / VIBRATING / HIGH
REPETITION RATE\nSigned X / Y / Z → frequency analysis\nShow dominant hertz (Hz; say: hurts) only when the signal passes quality checks

These paths share gravity-removed readings; Hz is not calculated from the smoothed graph. Raw axes are also displayed unchanged. Peak excludes startup warm-up. The accelerometer measures the phone itself, so it must be coupled to the surface.
Fresh, valid reading\nVisual: displacement in pixels (px; say: PIK-suhlz)\nPhysical: current smoothed g (standard gravity; say: jee)
Alerts enabled + armed + cooldown finished?\nReading ≥ your threshold?\nYES: trigger once · NO: keep monitoring
Show the alert message\nOptional alert sound (up to 2.5 seconds)\nOptional phone vibration
Wait 3 seconds\nThen a fresh reading below 90% of the threshold rearms that channel\nReturn to checking incoming readings

Sound or vibration disarms both channels because feedback can affect both measurements. Each then needs its own low reading after cooldown. Stop or background the app → stop monitoring and feedback, clear readings and graphs. Alerts default to off; thresholds are not safety limits.
Monitoring uses both camera and accelerometer on every tab.
Open Visual to check camera access before starting.
Say: peek\nHighest smoothed reading since reset
g (say: jee) expresses acceleration in multiples of standard gravity, not grams. 1 g ≈ 9.81 m/s² (meters per second squared). A still phone should settle near 0 g here because gravity is removed.
Includes gravity. X (ex), Y (why), Z (zed) are directions fixed to the phone, separate from the marker’s image position. m/s² measures acceleration; m² means square meters and measures area.

Based on root mean square (RMS; say: ar-em-ess):
NORMAL: below %1$.2f g
VIBRATING: %1$.2f g to below %2$.2f g
HIGH: %2$.2f g or above
g = multiples of standard gravity (say: jee).
Prototype thresholds · uncalibrated, not safety limits.

g (say: jee) is acceleration relative to standard gravity, not grams. Read m/s² as meters per second squared. 1 g = 9.80665 m/s²; 0.10 g ≈ 0.98 m/s². It describes how quickly velocity changes, not distance or vibration frequency.

Distance from the first tracked marker position, measured in camera pixels (px; say: PIK-suhlz), not screen pixels or millimeters. Losing the marker or restarting sets a new reference. Keep the phone steady: camera movement also changes this reading.
Marker position X / Y (say: ex / why)
Marker coordinates in the full, unrotated camera image. These are absolute image positions, not movement amounts or phone sensor axes. Their directions may differ from the rotated preview.

Smoothed magnitude of the phone’s acceleration after estimated gravity is removed, in g (standard gravity; say: jee). A still phone should settle near zero. This measures the phone’s motion; moving a remote object alone does not make the phone vibrate. Tilting the phone can briefly affect this reading.

RMS means root mean square (say: ar-em-ess): the overall vibration level over the latest %1$.1f second(s), in g. Computed as the square root of the average squared, unsmoothed acceleration magnitudes after gravity removal. RMS drives the status label.

Peak (say: peek) is a word, not an abbreviation. It means the highest smoothed magnitude since the session started or the analyzer reset, in g. The first %1$.1f seconds are excluded for warm-up. This is not the raw impact peak. RMS uses unsmoothed samples, so it can sometimes exceed this smoothed peak.
Raw acceleration X / Y / Z (ex / why / zed)

Measured in meters per second squared (m/s²; read the full unit aloud), including gravity. In the phone’s natural portrait orientation: +X points right, +Y toward the top, +Z out of the screen. Axes stay fixed to the phone as the display rotates. Lying still face-up, values should be roughly X = 0, Y = 0, Z = +9.81 m/s².

Each shows the latest 10 seconds using its own timestamps. Visual history shows displacement in px; physical history shows smoothed acceleration in g. Vertical scales adjust automatically, so equal graph heights do not mean equal motion. Visual gaps indicate missing tracking; reacquisition starts from a new reference. Stop or backgrounding clears both histories. These graphs do not show frequency. The separate dominant-frequency card estimates the phone’s vibration in Hz; distance in millimeters (mm; say: MIL-ih-mee-terz) is not measured.

Sensor sampling requests %1$d samples per second; the actual rate depends on the device. Physical readings refresh up to 10 times per second; visual readings up to 15. Gravity estimation uses a %2$.2f second filter time constant; magnitude smoothing uses %3$.2f seconds. Slow motion can be partly removed with gravity. A sensor gap longer than %4$.1f seconds or a backwards timestamp resets the analyzer, including peak. Restarting monitoring also resets it.
— means no valid reading is available. 0.00 is rounded to two decimal places and may include small motion or sensor noise. More decimal places do not imply calibrated accuracy.
